      Reaches

      —

      Filled boxes are entry points — where the outside world comes in. There are 34 of them and they are the reading order: 6 reached from a pointer or wheel event, 3 from a key press, 19 from a control in the interface, 4 components React mounts for a route, and 2 the browser itself calls. Every one was found by reading the source — a call inside a registered listener, inside a JSX handler prop, or inside an effect the interface drives — not by picking the ones that looked important.

      Grey boxes are test-only, and three boxes are struck through. 27 functions have no production caller at all; a suite is the only thing that depends on them, which is a real constraint on changing them and worth seeing. The struck-through three are the ones nothing in src/ names at all: Document.canRedo, LevelMap._edge and curvePerimeter.minDist — all three resolved in the 2026-08-31 cleanup: the first was wired up to grey the toolbar's Undo and Redo buttons, the other two deleted.

      Faint lines stay inside one file; solid ones leave it. That is the distinction worth drawing at this scale. A block whose edges are nearly all faint is self-contained — scaleBar/catalog, clipperOutline — and a block with a spray of solid lines leaving it is where the coupling lives. KobinEngine is the obvious one, and it is the reason the first item on the backlog is splitting it up.

      Nothing on this page calls 278 of these functions, and three of them are genuinely unused. Not the other 278. A call is only drawn when it resolves to a definite target; anything else is dropped rather than guessed at, so no incoming line means not proven, never not there. Click a function with a dashed outline and the panel says which case it is. The breakdown:

      Why there is no lineCountWhat it actually means
      passed as value107Exported, passed as a callback, or held somewhere — named without being called at a site the extractor reads.
      called via an object105Reached as thing.method() on a value whose type is not resolvable from the source. EventLatency.report is one: the hook calls eng.eventLatency.report().
      React component24React renders it as <Component/>. It is never called by name.
      getter15get inScale() and friends are read, not called, so there is no call syntax anywhere to find.
      test only26Nothing in the running app reaches it; a suite does. clipperOutline.clipPolysToRect is one, and its own file header says so.
      language protocol1toJSON. JSON.stringify invokes it by protocol, with the name appearing nowhere.
      no reference at all0A function that appears exactly once in src/, at its own definition. The 2026-08-31 cleanup cleared the list; anything appearing here is new.

      373 of the edges were also read off the source by hand, and the extractor independently finds 327 of those — which is the check on whether it is reading calls correctly rather than plausibly.

      Blocks with a dashed outline are not running, and are hidden until you ask for them. They are 186 of the functions here — the retired KobinEngineV0, the cubic-pipeline curvePerimeter, the polyline strokeShape, and the rest of src/engine/__oracles__/: independent implementations the shipping code is checked against, reachable only from test suites, so webpack has never bundled any of it. They are on this page because they are in the repository and the promise here is that every function is; they lay out below everything live so that hiding them costs the rest of the graph nothing. The four dev routes that used to sit alongside them were deleted on 2026-08-31.

      Every function in src/ outside the test suites, and every call that can be read off the source. 1,859 of the calls carry a file:line for the call site, so any line here can be checked against the code. Laid out offline — files layered by the calls between them, functions ordered inside each file by its own calls — so the page ships static SVG and no layout library.
